NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)  
The intervention is a periodic microcurrent reversal schedule applied during float charge to reverse the net corrosion current on the positive grid. Standard practice applies constant 2.27 V/cell float charge, causing continuous anodic dissolution of the lead grid. The adjacent-technique clearance is equalization charging, which briefly raises voltage to >2.4 V/cell to desulfate but accelerates corrosion; here, the reversal occurs at the same float voltage without exceeding it. The mechanism exploits the reversibility of lead corrosion electrochemistry: brief cathodic pulses at float voltage reduce Pb²⁺ back to Pb, netting zero cross-section loss over a duty cycle.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Driving variable = net anodic current density; the mechanism moves it down by reversing polarity (microampere/cm² pulses at float voltage), which reduces the failure driver by integrating to zero net dissolution over a cycle. The governing relation is Faraday’s law: Δm = (I·t·M)/(n·F), where reversing I for 10% of the cycle at same |t| yields net Δm ≈ 0.  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
Standard practice bill: (a) Float charger at 2.27 V/cell continuous.  
Intervention bill:  
1. (b) Commercial programmable timer, installed on charger control output, set to 15 min on / 2 h off (duty cycle 11%).  
2. (c) Timer output wired to reverse polarity relay coil (existing charger relay repurposed for bidirectional switching).  
3. (b) Standard DPDT relay (catalog class: 24 V DC coil, 30 A contacts), installed across battery terminals, wired for polarity reversal.  
4. (c) Charger setpoint unchanged at 2.27 V/cell; timer modulates relay to reverse battery polarity during off periods.  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installation: Timer/relay added (2 catalog parts) vs. none in standard; same electrician labor class.  
- Commissioning: Timer programming (15 min/2 h cycle) vs. none in standard; same technician time.  
- Operation: No additional energy (relay coil power negligible); no operational loss (float charge maintained).  
- Maintenance: Relay contacts (standard replacement interval) vs. none in standard; same class.  
Conclusion: Same burden class (infrastructure unchanged, labor parity).  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Deploy 10 identical VRLA batteries (2% Sb grids) with/without intervention. Float at 2.27 V/cell (25°C). Measure grid cross-section loss via micro-CT at 0, 5, 10, 15 years. Pass/fail: Cross-section loss < 15% at 15 years. Kill criterion: >20% loss at any interval. Duration: 15-year accelerated test (1.5× voltage, 40°C).  

MECHANISM CLASS: Electrochemical current reversal.
